selection.rationale: inputs/search.json allows only execution_plan this round, and the prior trial's failure evidence points at exactly that level. trial-paired-repair-a selected a joint 40-group conv->BatchNorm epilogue boundary at all 20 sites; it passed quality (max_abs_error 6.9e-6 over 1001 logits, exact top-1) but was rejected for paired_gain_not_above_noise (paired gains +0.1419/-0.0716 ms against MAD-derived bounds 0.0331/0.0431 ms; candidate wall became bimodal, 1.1872 vs 1.4145 ms). The framework's per-group before/after CUDA evidence shows why the edit could not clear the bound: the fold removed the 43.84 us of aten.batch_norm kernel time, but the 20 convolutions re-ran with a bias epilogue under slower cudnn heuristic choices - 4dbe179ff990714f37f0d969 regressed 39.648->55.818 us and 6214ff32dc254755c8d920f5 was flat at 118.846->119.094 us - so inclusive CUDA time across the 20 replaced sites actually rose ~2.9 us (13.5 us of per-site savings vs 16.4 us of regressions), while the candidate added 20 per-repeat Python guard dispatches and +46.5 MB of resident folded weights (peak allocated 86,361,088 -> 132,884,480 B). A kernel-time-neutral, dispatch-adding edit cannot beat a 33-43 us noise bound, and that is a property of the regime, not of the fold's algebra. The measured structure of this frozen workload shows the regime: the complete-workload call 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0 covers 731.385 us of GPU work in 81 CUDA kernels (coverage: 81/81 associated), but reference wall latency_ms is 1.336024 - a ~605 us (45.3%) per-forward gap charged by the eager delivery mechanism: 188 op dispatches per repeat (119 nn.Module __call__ inversions plus 69 aten op invocations), dozens of 1-4 us kernels in stages 0-2 (e.g. 1.1-2.8 us ReLUs, 1.7-2.5 us residual add_s, 8-12 us convs) that CPU dispatch cannot feed at ~3.2 us of non-kernel wall time per dispatched op. The previous trial demonstrated both halves of the trap: local kernel-time edits of that scale (~44 us) vanish inside this gap plus noise, and a faster local kernel need not move latency_ms at all. The coherent editable boundary is therefore the whole timed forward, selected at the two nested spans the framework targets and which enclose the identical 731.385 us region: the complete-workload group 3c57c8731ec33ed76cbb (project.invoke, 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0) and the ResNetForImageClassification group 6870b4a6e1536342a2ef (model forward, 80ff8693d7ac3cf2433b10f2, pixel_values [1,3,224,224] fp32 cuda). affected_calls is the entire subtree of that invoke: every observed module call, every aten call, and the instrumentation calls interleaved among them - 269 calls in all - because re-planning execution at this level changes the delivery of every one of them and none of them should be individually re-edited. The opportunity is to change how the frozen kernel DAG is delivered per repeat, not which kernels run: capture the unchanged eager forward once at build time (warmup and capture on a side stream into static input/output buffers), then per timed repeat copy the adapter's pixels into the static input, replay the captured graph, and return the static logits (cloned). The exact kernel sequence, FP32/TF32-off, cudnn-benchmark-off policies and the real fixture values are preserved, so no call is reordered, no alias or persistent state is introduced, and unknown cross-stream dependencies are respected by keeping the captured stream DAG identical to the eager one; any input not matching the captured shape/stride/dtype/device signature falls back to the unmodified eager forward. Per-op kernel work stays out of this round on purpose: the stage-3 conv inefficiency is real (bcb576ff7b303e075fb61f51, 256->512 stride-2 3x3, 115.966 us at ~1.0 TFLOP/s vs 30.848/36.544 us for its same-FLOP 115.6 MF stride-2 siblings 85e362c8893edef501c6b5c8/52801fdcf001973dc9b22a3b, plus c2db48d097463651f51bd75c, the three 512x512x3x3 @7x7 convs, 204.125 us at ~3.4 TFLOP/s vs ~19.0 us each for same-FLOP convs at 28x28; together 43.8% of region GPU time), but it belongs to per-op scopes that are not allowed here, and the rejected trial is direct evidence that such local gains do not by themselves move the project metric.
selection.hypothesis: Replacing the per-repeat eager dispatch of the frozen batch=1 FP32 forward with a build-time-captured whole-forward execution (one capture of the unchanged model(pixel_values=...).logits sequence on a side stream; per timed repeat: copy the fixed pixels into the static input, graph replay, clone/observe the static logits) removes most of the ~605 us per-forward non-kernel wall cost of 188 eager op dispatches and 81 kernel launches while executing the identical kernel DAG on identical input values, so logits and top-1 are expected to reproduce the reference exactly (same kernels, same order, deterministic cudnn heuristics with benchmark off) and paired median latency_ms is expected to fall from ~1.336 ms to ~0.75-0.90 ms, i.e. paired gains of roughly 0.4-0.55 ms in both AB and BA pairings - an order of magnitude above the 0.033-0.043 ms noise bounds that rejected the previous candidate. This is a hypothesis to be tested, not assumed: capture must prove capture-safe for this forward (conv/batch_norm/relu/pool/add_/linear/flatten only, no host syncs or .item() in the timed path); the static-input copy and output clone (~10-30 us) are real costs that must stay small; the graph's private memory pool must not materially regress peak_allocated_bytes from the 86,361,088 B baseline (the previous candidate's +46.5 MB shows the memory check bites); and worker-side one-time capture must stay outside the timed region in fresh AB/BA workers. Acceptance requires both paired gains above their MAD-derived noise bounds with logits within atol=rtol=1e-4, exact top-1, and math_policy_unchanged; any capture failure, tolerance failure, memory regression, or gain not above noise triggers atomic fallback to the unmodified eager execution.

proposal.rationale:
Previous feedback (inputs/previous-feedback.txt, trial-paired-repair-a) shows the concrete failure to repair: the joint conv->BatchNorm epilogue fold passed quality (max_abs_error 6.9e-6 over 1001 logits, exact top-1) but was rejected for paired_gain_not_above_noise - paired gains +0.1419/-0.0716 ms against MAD-derived bounds 0.0331/0.0431 ms, with a bimodal candidate wall (1.1872 vs 1.4145 ms). The framework's per-group CUDA evidence explains why it could not clear the bound: the fold removed 43.84 us of aten.batch_norm kernel time but the 20 convolutions re-ran with a bias epilogue under slower cudnn heuristic choices (-13.5 us of savings vs +16.4 us of regressions, net ~+2.9 us inclusive CUDA), while adding 20 per-repeat Python guard dispatches and +46.5 MB resident folded weights. A kernel-time-neutral, dispatch-adding edit cannot beat a 33-43 us wall-noise bound, and that regime property - not the fold's algebra - is what must be attacked.

This attempt therefore changes the delivery mechanism itself at the execution_plan scope search.json allows this round, using exactly the two nested spans the selection targets (complete-workload group 3c57c8731ec33ed76cbb / project.invoke 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0 and model group 6870b4a6e1536342a2ef / forward 80ff8693d7ac3cf2433b10f2, which enclose the identical 731.385 us region). The measured structure is: 731.385 us of GPU work in 81 CUDA kernels against a 1.336024 ms reference wall - a ~605 us (45.3%) per-forward gap charged by eager delivery (188 op dispatches per repeat: 119 nn.Module __call__ inversions plus 69 aten invocations, dozens of 1-4 us kernels at ~3.2 us non-kernel wall per dispatched op). The candidate captures the unchanged forward once at build time into static buffers (warmup on a side stream, then torch.cuda.graph capture of the model(pixel_values=static_input).logits sequence with all numerical policies untouched: FP32, TF32 off, cudnn benchmark off). Per timed repeat it copies the adapter's pixels into the static input, replays the identical captured kernel DAG on the current values, and returns a fresh clone of the static logits wrapped exactly like the parent (a dict with key "logits" at the project boundary, ImageClassifierOutput(loss=None, logits=...) at the model boundary). The workload's kernels execute on every invocation; nothing about the fixture answer is cached.

Expected effect: the 81 kernel launches and 188 Python dispatches collapse to one D2D copy, one graph replay and one 4 KB clone (~10-25 us of CPU-side work), so paired median latency_ms should fall from ~1.336 ms to ~0.75-0.90 ms - paired gains of roughly 0.4-0.55 ms in both AB and BA pairings, an order of magnitude above the 0.0331/0.0431 ms bounds that rejected the previous candidate. Numerics: replay re-executes the same kernels with the same parameters and deterministic cudnn heuristics (benchmark off), so logits are expected bitwise identical; a build-time two-input verification (fixture pixels and a flipped probe, proving the static-input copy genuinely feeds values) gates allclose at atol=rtol=5e-6 plus exact argmax and aborts atomically to parent passthrough on any mismatch, capture failure, signature mismatch or runtime error, so quality cannot degrade below the parent.

Coverage design: the project replacement routes through state["model"](pixel_values=...) so the installed model-forward replacement executes on every run and both returned call sites are live; if the module forward is demonstrably not routed to our replacement, the first call pays one eager forward (absorbed by warmup) and later calls switch to an inline replay path, preserving the gain either way. The remaining 267 affected calls (the subtree below the model forward: every nn.Module invocation, every aten op, and the profiler instrumentation calls) are eliminated by replay and listed in eliminated_calls; their consumers remain valid because the only observed consumers are the .logits attribute access in _infer and result["logits"] in observe, both served with fresh tensors, and the profiler _record_function calls only exist inside profiling diagnostics, never in the unprofiled measured run. No batch, sequence length, sampling semantics, data, generation count, dtype or threshold is changed; no inner call is individually re-edited, so the per-op conv hot spots intentionally remain for a future per-op round.

setup_work.description: One-time, build-phase only, executed in the worker before validation and outside every timed region; nothing runs per repeat except copy, replay and clone.
steps: Normalize device index; allocate static_input (empty_like of adapter pixels, created under inference_mode(False)) and copy the adapter pixels in.
3 warmup forwards of the unchanged model on a side stream under inference_mode, then synchronize (cudnn algo selection is deterministic: benchmark off).
torch.cuda.CUDAGraph capture of the unchanged model(pixel_values=static_input) forward under inference_mode; the captured .logits tensor is retained as the static output.

Verification outside any timed region: replay with the fixture pixels and with a flipped copy (input-dependence proof), each compared to a fresh eager forward at atol=rtol=5e-6 plus exact argmax; static input restored; cached eager blocks released with empty_cache.
Any failure at any step returns parent-equivalent passthrough replacements for both call IDs (atomic fallback).
setup_work.estimated_cost: ~6-8 forward passes (~10 ms GPU time) per worker process, one-time.
setup_work.memory: Graph private pool retains roughly one forward's transient activation working set (~41-42 MB at batch=1), plus static input 602,112 B and static logits 4,000 B; weights (44.5 MB) were already resident. Per-repeat allocations are a single 4,000 B logits clone, so timed peak_allocated_bytes is expected to sit at approximately the 86,361,088 B baseline (weights + activation working set), i.e. ~+0.6 MB rather than the previous trial's +46.5 MB. The build-time transient peak (~130 MB) occurs before adapter.reset() resets peak statistics and never enters a timed sample.
setup_work.state_lifecycle: Model parameters and buffers are never transformed; the model stays in eval mode; adapter.reset() (model.eval + peak-stat reset) remains valid before and after every repeat; the graph, static buffers and closures live for the worker process lifetime and are never refreshed per repeat; state["pixels"] is re-read and re-copied on every invocation, so changed pixel values flow through replay.
setup_work.synchronization: Capture happens on a non-default stream via torch.cuda.graph after side-stream warmup and an explicit synchronize; per repeat, copy_ -> graph.replay() -> clone are stream-ordered on the caller's current stream and complete before the harness's surrounding torch.cuda.synchronize(); no cross-stream dependencies are introduced at replay time and no host syncs occur inside the replacement.

quality_risks: Replay divergence from eager: mitigated by build-time two-input verification (fixture + flipped probe) at atol=rtol=5e-6 with exact argmax; identical kernels, order and deterministic cudnn heuristics (benchmark off, TF32 off) make bitwise equality the expected outcome, and any mismatch aborts to parent passthrough.

Memory regression: the graph pool could in principle exceed the eager transient working set; expected timed peak is ~baseline+0.6 MB, far below the +46.5 MB that accompanied the previous trial, and per-repeat allocations are one 4 KB clone.

Capture safety: the forward contains only conv2d/batch_norm/relu/max_pool/adaptive_avg_pool/add/flatten/linear, no host syncs, .item() or data-dependent control flow; capture failure is caught and degrades atomically to passthrough (zero gain, zero quality loss).

Aliasing/state: the static logits are cloned per call and output containers are freshly constructed, so no caller retains memory that a later replay overwrites; adapter state is only read, never mutated.

Signature scope: replacements apply only to the observed compatible signature (pixel_values [1,3,224,224] fp32 cuda contiguous, requires_grad False, no extra args/kwargs; project state with matching pixels); anything else falls back to the parent bound forward or adapter.run.

Contingency for a non-patching installer: if routing through state["model"] demonstrably does not reach the installed replacement, exactly one eager forward executes before switching to the inline replay path; the harness's 2 warmup repeats absorb it and medians are unaffected.
Wall-clock: if graph replay does not actually reduce delivery cost on the bound worker, the paired-gain gate rejects the candidate without any quality risk.
